title: solid-pod-guard: loopbackMappedFetch downgrades https->http for caller's own WebID, breaks real-HTTPS loopback issuers
description: SECURITY-CRITICAL upstream fix in jeswr/solid-sdk @jeswr/solid-pod-guard. resolveAuthorizedPod's loopbackMappedFetch (under allowInsecureLoopback) unconditionally rewrites https://<loopback> -> http://<loopback> when fetching the CALLER's own WebID document. But a dev/test issuer that runs a REAL HTTPS listener (required because the sparq pod's native OIDC verifier @solid/access-token-verifier has no loopback http exception for the pod-direct path) then receives a plain-http request at a TLS-only listener -> 'fetch failed' -> 502 pod_access. This blocks the lending journey e2e scenes 1(reissue)/3/4/5 (any createPodRouteGuard route called with the borrower identity). Fix options: (a) make the loopback downgrade scheme-aware — probe/prefer https for loopback WebIDs served over TLS, or make it configurable; (b) app-level ownerSeams rework so caller-WebID resolution bypasses the downgrade. Prefer (a) upstream. Must go through the pod-guard security bar (adversarial review + roborev claude-security lane) since it touches the allowInsecureLoopback boundary. After the SDK fix, re-vendor the tgz into solid-lending and re-run the journey e2e. Discovered from sm-qz3j.8.

title: SECURITY: assertAllowedPodBase accepts query/fragment → profile-card backward-ack bypass (all pod-route apps)
description: HIGH, found via the sm-75 pod-guard extraction review. apps/lender-boa/lib/server/pod.ts assertAllowedPodBase validates userinfo/https/allowlist but NEVER rejects a URL query (?x) or fragment (#x), returning url.href (query+fragment retained) + '/'. owner.ts then builds '<pod>profile/card' e.g. https://allowlisted-host/x#y/profile/card; on fetch the fragment is stripped so the HTTP read hits https://allowlisted-host/x, NOT the owner-only-writable profile card. A webid can set its own pim:storage to such a URL on an allowlisted host and defeat the bidirectional backward-acknowledgment binding (decision-0015 L2). Latent in the live demo only because pod routes 503 until sm-2eg (service identity) is wired, but a real boundary bug. FIX: reject any pod URL carrying search or hash → PodAccessError(400) before allowlist/return, in EVERY pod-route app's copy of this helper (lender-boa, and the copies/shared use in gse, verifications, wallet, closing, property). Add tests (pod ?x / #x / #x/profile/card confusion ⇒ 400). The canonical fix is landing in @jeswr/solid-pod-guard (sm-75); mirror it here or adopt pod-guard (sm-77).
close_reason: SECURITY HIGH fixed via PR #33: assertAllowedPodBase now rejects ?query/#fragment (incl. bare separators) with 400 in both canonical copies (lender-boa, property; other pod-route apps import lender-boa's), closing the profile-card backward-ack bypass. title: vc-kit seed-tooling mintOperandAnchors native bridge breaks Turbopack bundling (wallet Mode-1)
description: Low/framework. @lending/vc-kit/seed-tooling (mintOperandAnchors native bridge) resolves a filesystem path in a way that breaks Turbopack bundling of the wallet Mode-1 route — same reason solid-mortgage's wallet worker avoids it. Seeder worked around with a direct issueCredential carrying the captured encoding (functionally identical signed output). Make the anchor-minting path bundler-safe (browser-safe subpath). surface:packages/vc-kit.

title: design-doc + sm-77: framework is domain-GENERIC (no built-in insigniaPreset/us-finance roster)
description: Lead directive 2026-07-17: the public showcase framework must be in no way finance-specific — a generic multistakeholder pod-data walkthrough. sm-75 kit accordingly REMOVED the insigniaPreset concept + us-finance roster entirely; brandingConfigSchema has no insigniaPreset field; consumers supply their own bannedMarks. This deviates from showcase-framework-design.md §3.2 (which had an insigniaPreset: us-finance enum). Update the design doc §3.2/§3.3 to reflect the domain-generic decision, and ensure sm-77 (solid-mortgage adoption) carries the US-finance banned-marks roster + the mortgage-exact golden vectors in the PRIVATE repo. Discovered in sm-75 kit domain-generic round.

title: pod-guard + source: allowInsecureLoopback disables the SSRF guard for ALL destinations, not just loopback
description: Medium, dev-only, inherited from owner.ts. When allowInsecureLoopback is enabled (dev/e2e only), the guarded/DNS-pinned profile fetch is replaced with plain fetch for EVERY destination — so a non-loopback WebID could reach private/link-local HTTPS without SSRF protection. Never set in prod, so not a live risk, but the flag should ONLY relax the guard for actual loopback targets. Fix in @jeswr/solid-pod-guard (canonical) and mirror to the solid-mortgage source (apps/lender-boa/lib/server/owner.ts + copies). From sm-75 pod-guard roborev general (job 27).

title: e2e journey: retry/isolation safety — destructive shared-pod mutation fails on retry/rerun
description: e2e/journey.spec.ts destructively mutates the shared seeded pod assuming pristine state. Serial mode doesn't isolate it from other specs, and a Playwright retry reuses the already-mutated global fixture — a retry after scene 5 fails immediately (closing record already exists → 409); concurrent readers can see transient/deleted data. Currently green (no retry needed) but makes the suite non-retry-safe. IMPORTANT before sm-59 relies on this journey. Fix: provision/reseed a journey-specific pod per worker+retry, or isolate the project and reset mutated resources before rerun. From sm-36 roborev general (job 21).

title: e2e journey: acknowledge BoA/GSE interstitials before scene-3/4 clicks (flake risk)
description: e2e/journey.spec.ts scenes 3-4 click Submit application / Run underwriting / Run freshness check without first calling acknowledgeInterstitial/dismissInterstitialIfPresent; the modal CAN intercept and time out (each test gets a fresh context). Currently green but a latent flake. Fix: acknowledge the interstitial after each relevant navigation before interacting. From sm-36 roborev general (job 21).

title: solid-kit dev-issuer: first-class deferred/settable storage claim (setStorage seam)
description: sm-36's e2e global-setup relies on the dev issuer reading options.storage per-request to break the issuer<->pod boot circularity (seed a borrower identity, boot pod with that owner). Fragile. Add a first-class solid-kit dev-issuer seam to set/defer the pim:storage claim after construction. From sm-36 journey e2e.

title: seeder: native dual-sign witness test verifies formats only, not Schnorr signature/commitment/binding
description: test/mortgage-seed-integration.test.ts native rail test checks witness FIELD FORMATS but never verifies the Schnorr signature, commitment, or binding to the seeded credential+anchor — an invalid or swapped witness could pass. The seeded witnesses ARE real (real sm-26 Schnorr-BJJ dual-sign), but the test doesn't cryptographically re-verify them. Fix: run the native verification/proof round-trip and assert cryptographic validity + credential/field binding. Relates to running the native rail in CI. From sm-65 fix roborev general (job 20).

title: CI: run the native-rail (Schnorr witness) ACL-denial test on REAL witnesses
description: sm-65 FIX 1's OIDC witness-denial proof runs on real witnesses only when SPARQ_CHECKOUT is present (the native dual-sign rail). In CI (no rail) the witness resource is materialized via plumbing-fake issuance (existence only, no faked crypto) to test the ACL. To prove owner-only ACL on a REAL Schnorr-BJJ witness in CI, the native rail (Rust+nargo toolchain, pinned sparq checkout) must run in CI — see sm-2ic (native seed-tooling CI job). Extend that job to run the gated native witness-denial test. Discovered in sm-65 ACL hardening.

title: Revisit Vercel deploy gating if legal (sm-5q2) / consent (sm-6sw) requires an auth wall
description: DECISION 2026-07-17 (Jesse): production .vercel.app demo surfaces are left PUBLIC, mitigated by noindex + robots.txt Disallow + concept-demo disclaimers (all confirmed live). On the Hobby plan Vercel Authentication cannot gate production. If the sm-5q2 legal review or sm-6sw Freddie consent concludes an auth wall is required, apply one of: (1) DELETE each <project>.vercel.app production domain so only SSO-gated team aliases serve, or (2) upgrade to Vercel Pro and set ssoProtection deploymentType=all. Runbook in docs/deploy.md 'Deployment protection'.

title: Configure MORTGAGE_*_SERVICE_WEBID for deployed pod-route apps against a live pod host
description: The 9 zones are deployed (sm-37) but every pod-route app (wallet, lender-a/boa, lender-b/53, underwriting/gse, verifications, property, closing) fails CLOSED — 503 on its pod API routes — until its service-identity env (MORTGAGE_*_SERVICE_WEBID + client-credentials, see each app's lib/server/config.ts) is set against a live Solid pod host. Needs the Mode-2 host (sm-52) provisioned first. Then set the service env on each Vercel project (production+preview) and redeploy. Until then the live demo can render UI but authenticated pod flows return 503.

title: verifications: resume-path leaks superseded orphan-anchor status index (residual allocator exhaustion)
description: After a failed main-credential write leaves a committed orphan anchor, each retry allocates+overwrites the anchor with a NEW index, leaving the superseded anchor index occupied — so repeatedly allowing anchor writes while rejecting credential writes can still slowly exhaust the finite per-flow allocator despite FIX G's confirmed-failure releases. Security lane judged it below the exploitability bar (rate-limited 60/burst 1/s, large Bitstring space, self-tenant). Fix: validate+REUSE the correct orphan anchor's existing index during resume rather than minting a fresh one. From sm-29 r3 roborev general (job 16). Related to per-process allocator demo-scope limit.

title: verifications: flows dashboard reports verified:true from main credential only, ignoring anchor state
description: The flows endpoint marks an anchored flow verified:true based solely on the main credential; a missing/revoked/malformed/wrong-field ANCHOR is ignored even though that flow cannot support its advertised ZK proof path. Happy-path accurate (anchors always valid), but the status over-reports readiness in edge states (demo-integrity). Fix: read+validate required anchors with the same issuer/subject/status/field/encoding checks (reuse assessAnchorRenewal) and fold into the flow's verified+fresh state. From sm-29 r3 roborev general (job 16).

title: verifications: durable recovery for a revoked-but-present credential (process death between revoke and reinstate)
description: If the process dies between reissueCredential's index revoke and the compensating reinstate, the old index stays revoked while the old credential is still pod-resident. It fails SAFE (verifies REVOKED) but the borrower is locked out of both reissue (refuses already-revoked) and issue (409 already_issued). Inherent to non-transactional multi-store writes. Add a durable journal / repair path for a revoked-but-present credential. From sm-29 adversarial re-review.

title: verifications: verify issuer service token WebID matches configured serviceWebId (L4 attribution)
description: getPodFetch never uses config.serviceWebId/options.serviceWebId, so an unset expected service WebID does not fail closed and client credentials resolving to a different principal aren't detected despite the documented decision-0015 L4 identity binding. Same class as gse sm-4oq. Fix: require the configured service WebID and validate the client-credentials identity matches before pod ops; cover missing+mismatched in boundary tests. From sm-29 hardening roborev general (job 10).

title: gse: canonicalZip rejects conflicting ZIP+4 suffixes in appraisal property binding
description: loan-file.ts sameSubjectProperty/canonicalZip discards ZIP+4 even when BOTH addresses carry a suffix, so 43004-1111 and 43004-9999 pass the property binding. Narrow (needs a verified, subject-bound appraisal for a different property in the same 5-digit ZIP) but slightly weakens the sm-32 FIX-3 binding. Fix: when both addresses have a ZIP+4, require the suffixes to match; compare only the 5-digit prefix when one lacks a suffix; test conflicting ZIP+4. From sm-32 fix3 roborev general (job 11).

title: data-model: give PropertyShape a first-class property IRI/parcel identifier (not blank node)
description: mshape:PropertyShape currently mints property nodes as blank nodes (data-model build.ts, vc-kit claims.ts), so gse's appraisal-to-application binding (sm-32 FIX 3) had to fall back to a canonicalized postal-address comparison — no stable identifier exists on either the LoanApplication.subjectProperty or AppraisalCredential subjectProperty. Add a stable property IRI or parcel/APN identifier to PropertyShape + the vocab, so property binding can be exact rather than address-heuristic. Then tighten gse loan-file.ts sameSubjectProperty to compare the identifier. Discovered fixing sm-32 appraisal-property binding.

title: gse: verify AUS service token WebID matches configured serviceWebId (creator attribution)
description: aus-rail.ts serviceWebId is configured independently of the client credentials used by createServicePodFetch, with no check that the resulting access token represents that WebID. A misconfiguration could write a decision falsely attributed to another service identity. Two security reviews confirmed serviceWebId is creator-attribution only (not a security gate), so this is integrity/correctness hardening, not a boundary hole. Fix: derive the creator from the authenticated service token, or verify the service-fetch token WebID against serviceWebId; add a mismatched-config test. From sm-32 roborev general (job 7).

title: data-model + gse: persist full AUS findings as RDF into the pod
description: gse currently writes only the decision document (status, recommendation, approved amount, conditions quoting failed findings) to the pod; the full per-rule findings report lives only in the API response. Inline RDF persistence is blocked because mshape:UnderwritingDecisionShape is sh:closed and @mortgage/data-model has no findings shape/vocab. Add a findings shape + vocab terms in data-model, then have gse underwrite.ts write every finding (code, category, result, observation, rule, threshold) as SHACL-validated RDF (in the decision resource or a linked findings resource). Realizes the dual-delivery (lender + pod) fully. Discovered fixing sm-32 honesty finding.

title: tooling: per-app 'pnpm --filter <app> lint/test' fails (biome not found) without root node_modules/.bin on PATH
description: On this box, pnpm run <script> inside an app dir does NOT put the workspace-root node_modules/.bin on PATH, so per-app biome/gate invocations fail with 'biome: not found' unless prefixed with PATH=$PWD/node_modules/.bin:$PATH (root-level pnpm run lint works). Both sm-29 and sm-32 builders hit this. Risk: CI-parity checks that shell into an app dir. Investigate pnpm/turbo config; document or fix so per-app gates work uniformly.

title: gse: e2e negative-credential coverage (forged-signature, subject-mismatch, revoked-status)
description: The evidence gate (verified/subjectBound/fresh) is only unit-tested with injected flags. Add integration tests that plant, in a real pod, (a) a bad-signature credential, (b) a credential whose credentialSubject != borrower, (c) a revoked-status credential, and assert the REAL vc-kit verifier drives the run to refer each time. Closes the integration-coverage gap on verify gates. From sm-32 adversarial review.

title: gse: Mode-2b browser login UI (AUS console can't attach DPoP)
description: aus-console uses plain fetch; an authenticated browser Solid session can't drive the run (always 401). Same deferral as lender-boa sm-3qz. Acceptance: console runs an authenticated AUS request via the session's DPoP fetch; add a component-level authenticated-run test. Deferred from sm-32 merge.

title: verifications: Mode-2b browser login UI (issue/reissue panels can't attach DPoP)
description: The issue/reissue panels call protected endpoints with plain fetch, so browser sessions always 401 (roborev sm-29 High, functional). Same deferral pattern as lender-boa sm-3qz. Acceptance: a real Solid-OIDC browser session drives issue+reissue through a DPoP-capable authenticated fetch; panel already degrades honestly on 401. Deferred from sm-29 merge (security boundary + write atomicity landed).

title: wallet: cross-instance receipt-store reconciliation (readiness sentinel / shared lock)
description: roborev sm-28 round-7: the RECEIPT-STORE integrity races are now CLOSED at runtime by a readiness sentinel (apps/wallet/lib/grants/engine.ts READY_SENTINEL) — no shared lock needed, landed in sm-28. The store is marked ready ONLY after provision+lock+reconcile-clean; any transition on a locked-but-unmarked store fails closed (retryable 409). This closes: (a) the failed-reconcile retry-laundering (reachable SINGLE-instance via a transient DELETE-failure + one retry — round-6 mis-scoped it as cross-instance-only; corrected) and (b) the concurrent-instance legitimate-receipt misclassification, plus sweeps the nested-container-plant DoS into ordinary fail-closed. Regression: receipt-store-window.test.ts 'failed reconcile never marks ready, retry fails closed'. REMAINING scope of THIS bead: fold the sentinel into the GENERAL cross-instance transition lock (grant racing revoke across instances) — i.e. sm-9kz — so the whole rail (not just the receipt store) is multi-instance-safe. Lower priority now that the security-relevant receipt-store races are closed.

title: wallet/data-model: sign wallet consent receipts (cryptographic policy-record integrity)
description: roborev sm-28 round-3 residual: the /mortgage/receipts/ protected store + tamper-checked lock stops every NON-Control party from forging policy records, but a party holding acl:Control on /mortgage/ (the closing party, or any non-wallet Control grant) could pre-create the store, plant SHACL-valid forged receipts at deterministic vault IRIs, and install a matching owner+service-only lock — the wallet then trusts a frozen forged snapshot. WAC alone cannot prove a receipt was WALLET-written. Structural closure: sign wallet consent receipts (buildConsentReceipt → eddsa-rdfc-2022 via vc-kit issue path, wallet service key) and have readPolicyHistory verify the signature + issuer == wallet service before trusting a record for immutability/sequence. Complements the cross-surface least-privilege bead (remove closing's container Control). Until then the container-Control forge path is the documented residual; the demo's per-visitor Mode-1 pods + wallet-mediated Mode-2 flow (store always wallet-created first, before any party grant) do not reach it. Acceptance: a forged-but-unsigned policy record is ignored even inside a matching lock; regression test with a Control-holding attacker.

title: wallet+lender-boa+closing: least-privilege grant scoping (read-only container, writes to dedicated resources)
description: roborev sm-28 HIGH #1/#3 (codex + claude-security): the wallet's container grant materialises Write with acl:default on /mortgage/, so a write-granted lender's service identity can modify ANY member (credentials, anchors) and the closing party's Control lets it rewrite /mortgage/.acl wholesale — bypassing the app-level revocation invariant (WAC is the real enforcement). sm-28 ALREADY closed the receipt-integrity portion structurally (protected /mortgage/receipts/ subcontainer with an owner+service-only ACL overriding the container default; policy history reads only there; display ledger tolerant). The RESIDUAL is credential/anchor write-exposure + container-Control. Correct fix is cross-surface: (a) protect /mortgage/credentials/ + /mortgage/zk/ with read-only-for-parties ACLs the wallet sets; (b) move lender write-back (currently /mortgage/application + /mortgage/decision — RESOURCE_POD_PATHS, lender-boa/lib/server/loan.ts) into a dedicated writable output subcontainer and grant Write only there; (c) grant closing Control ONLY on the closing-record resource ACL, not the container. Touches wallet (grant modeling), lender-boa (write paths), closing (ACL management). Acceptance: negative tests prove a write-granted party cannot modify credentials/anchors nor rewrite the container ACL.

title: data-model/vc-kit: align persona ZK values with captured operand encodings
description: PERSONA_VALUES (income 8200 / score 745) have no captured sparq operand encodings; the wallet's Mode-1 seed (decision 0016) therefore issues its signed credentials with the vc-kit canonical demo values (8500/742 — captured, genuine). Invisible today (the wallet never displays raw hidden values) but a future surface printing both would expose the divergence. Fix either way: (a) extend DEMO_OPERAND_VALUES with 8200/745 and re-run capture-fixtures.mjs against the native toolchain (SPARQ_CHECKOUT + pinned nargo), or (b) change PERSONA_VALUES to 8500/742. Then update apps/wallet/lib/pod/seed.ts to use persona values directly.

title: wallet: Mode-1 pod lifetime across hard navigations/refresh
description: The per-visitor SharedWorker pod dies (and reseeds) when the LAST connected document unloads — a hard refresh or address-bar navigation in a single tab wipes granted ACLs + receipts. In-app nav is client-side so the demo journey holds, but a presenter refreshing mid-demo loses scene state. Options: persist the pod's resources to OPFS/IndexedDB and rehydrate on boot, or a keepalive strategy. Honesty copy must keep saying state never leaves the browser. Acceptance: refresh mid-journey retains the ledger, e2e-asserted.

title: vc-kit: e2e-verifiable Tier A transcripts (export low-level verifyProof via testing subpath)
description: The wallet e2e verifies browser-produced presentations out-of-band (nonce→challengeFieldOf binding, anchor-operand equality, flavour, size) but cannot re-run the UltraHonk verifier on the captured transcript in Node because zk/backend's verifyProof is unexported. Extend the sm-05j shared ZK test rig / testing subpath to expose it, then tighten e2e/wallet.spec.ts to cryptographically verify captured proofs. Acceptance: wallet e2e fails if the captured transcript is not a valid proof for its public inputs.

title: wallet: Mode-2b borrower login UI (real Solid-OIDC session for live grants + VP-POST)
description: The wallet's Mode-2 grant rail and the lender VP-POST rail are DPoP-authenticated and fully tested with real dev-issuer sessions, but the app ships no borrower login UI — the deployed demo runs only the disclosed Mode-1 client rail. Add a real Solid-OIDC login (solid-kit createAuthClient + stable Client Identifier Document per decision 0011) so grants and scene-2 presentations run live against hosted pods without test-injected headers. Same gap family as lender-boa's. Acceptance: login flow drives /api/grants + presentToLender with a real session in a Mode-2b e2e.

title: solid-sdk/solid-vc: browser-safe Bitstring status-list codec
description: solid-vc's encode/decodeStatusList uses node:zlib gzipSync/gunzipSync and Buffer base64url — both break under bundler browser polyfills (browserify-zlib rejects Uint8Array input; feross/buffer lacks base64url). The wallet (sm-28) carries scoped workarounds: a Buffer base64url patch (apps/wallet/lib/pod/buffer-base64url-patch.ts) and passing a Buffer-typed bitstring into StatusListClient.create. Upstream fix in jeswr/solid-vc: feature-detect (CompressionStream/DecompressionStream or pako fallback) + manual base64url codec; then drop the wallet patches. Jesse's repo — PR in-scope after lead approval.

title: Host the walkthrough JSON-Schema at a dereferenceable IRI
description: Per sm-73 design §2/§7: the walkthrough.v1.json schema artifact ships as a package subpath export only; a hosted $schema IRI is blocked on solid-sdk repo visibility (private repo raw URLs do not dereference; no minted IRIs at URLs that don't resolve — house rule). Acceptance: a public, stable, dereferenceable URL serving the schema (candidates: jeswr.github.io, jeswr.org path) + $schema field documented in @jeswr/solid-showcase SKILL.md + lint-iris-style HEAD check in solid-sdk CI. Needs Jesse's call on hosting surface.

title: Extract @jeswr/solid-browser-pod (Mode-1 in-browser pod runtime) upstream
description: Per sm-73 design §1.4/§7: packages/solid-kit/src/browser-pod (SharedWorker host, postMessage protocol, dedicated-worker fallback, simulated-login disclosure) is generic showcase infrastructure (decision 0011 Mode-1) but couples to the vendored sparq wasm tarball + patch — deliberately OFF the sm-74/75 critical path. Acceptance: package in jeswr/solid-sdk with SKILL.md; page-side client wasm-free/node-free as today; worker host's sparq dependency strategy resolved (vendored tarball vs published sparq artifact — prefer waiting for sparq GHCR/npm publish, sq-lmz40); mortgage consumes it in sm-77 or after.

title: Refactor solid-mortgage onto the showcase framework (first consumer)
description: Once sm-74/75/76 land: migrate solid-mortgage's tour + disclaimer + auth-boundary + deploy to consume the upstream showcase framework, proving the extraction and leaving mortgage as the reference use-case. Convert the tour pages to the JSON walkthrough document.

title: lender-53: shared atomic ZK verifier state for multi-instance deploy
description: The scene-2 verifier deliberately reuses lender-boa's process-local nonce, DPoP replay, and rate-limit stores. This fails closed for valid cross-instance challenges but does not provide deployment-wide replay/rate-limit state. Acceptance: inject shared atomic storage behind the existing solid-kit interfaces (single-use GETDEL-equivalent nonces plus shared DPoP jti replay and rate limiting), prove challenges minted on one instance verify exactly once on another, retain holder/anchor/issuer checks unchanged, and document the production env posture.

title: e2e: real SharedWorker browser-pod smoke test (Playwright)
description: The sm-23 browser-pod unit suite mocks the worker BOUNDARY (vitest cannot run a real SharedWorker) and drives the wasm dispatch handler directly. Add a Playwright e2e in a real browser that (a) boots the actual SharedWorker pod host from a bundled worker entry (proves the bundler resolves the --target web wasm asset via new URL(...,import.meta.url)), (b) does a seeded read + writable PUT/GET round-trip through browserPodFetch/connectBrowserPod, and (c) opens two tabs on the same origin and confirms they share ONE pod (per-visitor not per-tab). Acceptance: e2e suite green in CI against a bundled worker; covers the SharedWorker path the unit tests structurally cannot. Belongs with the first app that mounts the runtime (sm-28 wallet).

title: closing: shared cross-instance transition serialization
description: apps/closing/lib/server/scene.ts serializes close/servicing transitions per pod IN-PROCESS only (withPodTransitionLock). Across Vercel instances the backstop is conditional writes (If-Match / If-None-Match:*) + deterministic per-transition receipt IRIs, so races lose loudly and retry-repair converges — but a shared lock (e.g. Redis SET NX, same seam family as the solid-api-auth replay store and solid-kit nonce store) would remove the retry round-trips and the transient 5xx. Acceptance: shared lock behind the withPodTransitionLock seam OR a documented reconciliation proof + multi-writer test; roborev codex 616ad62 Low.

title: e2e/lender-boa.spec.ts: unused borrowerWebId lint warning
description: Biome warns lint/correctness/noUnusedVariables for 'borrowerWebId' at e2e/lender-boa.spec.ts:100 (pre-existing on main; surfaced while linting the sm-34 fix). Acceptance: warning gone, spec still green.

title: hoist decision-0015 boundary into solid-kit (extract-on-second-use)
description: apps/closing is the SECOND consumer of lender-boa's auth boundary (resolveAuthorizedPod, pod.ts IO, AuthenticatedPodCaller, the authenticate→overrides→body→bind pipeline) and today imports it cross-app (apps/closing/lib/server/{pod-rail,scene}.ts import ../../../lender-boa/lib/server/*). Decision 0015 prescribes hoisting the boundary + resolver into solid-kit unchanged on second use. Acceptance: shared modules live in packages/solid-kit (server-only subpath), lender-boa + closing consume them, no cross-app lib imports remain, gate green.

title: sm-34-fix: closing app production hardening (roborev High/Med)
description:
Address roborev findings on PR #22 (sm-34 closing app):
HIGH 1 - apps/closing/app/closing-experience.tsx:56 client requests send no Authorization/DPoP headers so real scene endpoints fail auth (Playwright hides this by intercepting requests); use authenticated Solid-OIDC fetch + integration test against real handlers.
HIGH 2 - apps/closing/lib/server/pod-rail.ts:86 services default to anonymousPodFetch so authenticated calls cannot read/write private WAC-protected pod resources; supply grant-authenticated service fetch (sm-28 seam).
HIGH 3 - apps/closing/lib/server/scene.ts:184 repeating close overwrites the closing record and unconditionally regrants lender access; after revocation a reload silently regrants with no receipt. Make close idempotent/immutable (409 on existing) and never regrant on repeat.
MED 4 - apps/closing/lib/server/scene.ts:200 ACL is mutated before the receipt is written; a failed receipt write changes access with no ledger record. Implement recoverable transition (pending/committed receipt or ACL compensation).
LOW 5 - packages/ui/src/app-shell.tsx:45 skip link targets #main-content but wallet/tour/lender consumers do not provide that id; have AppShell own the target wrapper or require the id across consumers.
notes:
SUPERSEDED by the in-flight Fable fix on bead/sm-34 (PR #22) — these are NOT optional demo-hardening: finding #3 (repeat-close silently regrants revoked lender access) is a real security bug that breaks scene 5's control thesis, and the e2e mocked the auth path so green tests didn't prove it. The Fable agent is fixing all 3 High + Med with real-auth e2e + an immutable-revocation regression test, gated on a clean claude-security verdict before merge. Close this when PR #22 merges clean.

RESOLVED on PR #22 head 8bfadac (6 review rounds): all 3 High + 1 Med + follow-on findings fixed; e2e mocking REMOVED (real DPoP auth end-to-end, property recipe); closing service identity = solid-kit createServicePodFetch (client_credentials+DPoP), no anonymous fallback (503 fail-closed); revocation immutable + regression-tested via real WAC reads at unit/route/e2e; receipt/ACL consistency with compensation+repair+collision validation; per-pod in-process serialization (sm-9kz tracks shared lock). VERDICTS on 8bfadac: codex clean + claude-security clean (3 consecutive clean security rounds). PR CI green (incl. e2e) since 3c8a207; Vercel deploy green. Close when PR #22 merges.

title: Persist verifications issuer keys and status lists across instances
description: The sm-29 concept runtime keeps issuer signing keys, Bitstring Status List documents, allocators, and re-issue state in process memory. Before a multi-instance deployment is presented as operational, move this registry to durable issuer-owned storage with atomic status updates and stable key loading; acceptance: credentials issued on one instance verify through status/key endpoints served by another, and concurrent revocations cannot be lost.

title: lender-boa: Mode-2b borrower login UI so the authenticated pod rail is driveable without test-injected headers
description: The scene-3/4 pages show honest demo/rail-off states when unauthenticated; the authenticated flow is only driveable via e2e DPoP header injection. Add a real Solid login (reactive-fetch per suite preference; stable Client Identifier Document) whose session fetch carries DPoP to the app's own /api routes, so Mode 2b visitors exercise decision 0015 end-to-end. Acceptance: login UX on /application + /freshness, prefill/submit/freshness work with the real session against the hosted-mode pod, honest states preserved when logged out.

title: lender-boa: wire the grant-authenticated lender service identity into the podIoFetch seam
description: Decision 0015 L4 consuming side is stubbed: lib/server/pod.ts pod IO defaults to an ANONYMOUS redirect-refusing fetch, proven (test/pod-auth.test.ts WAC suite) to fail closed against WAC pods. Once sm-28 lands the ODRL/DPV grant pipeline (WAC materialised for the lender WebID) + the lender's client-credential DPoP identity, inject that identity's fetch via the podIoFetch seam and extend the WAC test to prove the GRANTED read succeeds while the ungranted one still fails. SECURITY (roborev security job 5579, Low): the L2 backward acknowledgment assumes <pod>profile/card is owner-only-writable; once the lender fetch is PRIVILEGED, a forged acknowledgment on an allowlisted host permitting non-owner card writes would channel privileged IO into a victim's pod — when implementing, bind via the grant registry instead of the card where a grant exists, or add a fail-closed check/test that acknowledgment cards on allowlisted origins are not anonymously writable. description: Low. packages/solid-showcase-kit/src/testing/insignia.ts insigniaFindings second pass: lineOfChar is populated by code-point iteration (for..of) but indexed with match.index (UTF-16 code-unit offset). For text with astral characters before a cross-line match, the reported line number is misattributed (excerpt+detection are correct — only the line number). Fix: track lineOfChar in UTF-16 units. title: verifications: anchor repair re-derives operand from config, not the stored credential's asserted value

Safe today under pinned claims + signature verification (not attacker-exploitable), but fragile if an operator ever changes a flow's pinned value after issuance. Consider deriving the operand from the verified stored credential. From sm-29 adversarial re-review (Low).

title: solid-kit: readPodResource collapses a real 403 into PodAccessError(502)
description: pod.ts maps only 404->undefined; every other status (incl. 403 grant-denial) throws PodAccessError(502), forcing grant-denial tests to accept [403,502] and blurring deny semantics. Preserve the upstream status (esp. 403) so deny semantics + assertions are sharper. Cosmetic, not a security defect. From sm-32 adversarial review.

title: verifications: reissue TOCTOU cleanup (single re-read of the credential body)
description: reissueGate verifies a freshly re-read body while reissueCredential runs on the earlier resource.dataset read. Not exploitable (same authenticated fetch on the borrower's own pod; reissueCredential re-verifies proof/issuer/status internally) but a single read is cleaner. From sm-29 adversarial review.

title: vc-kit: status-list pod resource is opaque vc+ld+json — revisit RDF-native hosting
description: Why: the hosted BitstringStatusListCredential is PUT as application/vc+ld+json because the SSRF-guarded pod (correctly) refuses application/ld+json carrying the remote VC 2.0 @context, so the list is stored byte-exact/opaque rather than as queryable pod RDF (packages/vc-kit/src/status.ts LIST_CONTENT_TYPE comment). Verifiers consume it as JSON per the W3C spec, so nothing is broken - this is an RDF-discipline nicety. Options: pinned-context allowlist in the sparq server for https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2 (upstream, log in docs/research/lws-gaps.md), or an inline-context serialisation. Acceptance: decision recorded (or lws-gaps entry filed); if implemented, the hosted list parses as RDF on the pod AND still passes solid-vc's resolveBitstringStatus id/purpose/signature checks.

title: sparq: fail build:lws-wasm fast on wasm-pack < 0.14

Works on >= 0.14 (0.15.0 verified). Acceptance: packages/solid-server preflights the wasm-pack version (or README + guardrail states the minimum) so consumers get an actionable error instead of a cargo flag conflict.
